name: Unicly PointFarm deposit reenters through the ERC1155 points mint
summary: PointFarm.deposit(pid, amount) mints the caller's pending points as ERC1155 tokens with _mint, whose onERC1155Received callback runs before user.rewardDebt is updated, so a contract can re-enter deposit(pid, 0) and be paid the same pending points again. The attacker staked 3,528 uJENNY in the uJENNY pool on 2023-09-14, and two days later called deposit(0, 0) from a contract that re-entered twice, minting 3 x 3,528 points instead of 3,528; it withdrew its uJENNY, sold it back for 0.4968 WETH and redeemed 10,000 points in PointShop for the uJENNY shop's Realms NFT #4689.
notes: Reset is the listing of the uJENNY pool (pid 0; poolInfo[0].uToken and poolInfo length in slot 9), made through PointShop by 0x0ef024d2 at block 13558853, six days after PointFarm's deployment (0xc47d361b, block 13521372): the exploit needed that pool. Later PointFarm writes are the attacker's own preparatory deposit (0x782d6f77, block 18133172), user balances and accumulators (rule 8).

Earlier exploits: PointFarm's whole log history (19 events) shows only 0x0ef024d2's two deposits in November 2021 and the attacker's two transactions; no points were ever minted before the anchor, whose three TransferSingle mints of 3,528 points to the attack contract 0x9d9820f1 in one call are the reentrancy. No later exploit: no PointFarm event follows the anchor.

Loss is the Realms NFT #4689 that left PointShop, which has no fungible market price; it is valued at what the attacker realised (rule 12), 0.796 ETH from its Seaport sale for 0.8 ETH two days later (0x156c006b) at $1,639.17. The attacker's 3,528 uJENNY was its own deposit, withdrawn in the same transaction.
